title: U.S. House · Oregon's 1st District
area: Northwest Oregon, including Washington County suburbs of Portland (Hillsboro, Beaverton area), and the north Oregon coast (Astoria, Tillamook, Lincoln City).

context.text: Incumbent Suzanne Bonamici defeated Jamil Ahmad 86.6%-12.8% in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary. Barbara Kahl defeated John Verbeek 71.5%-27.4% in the Republican primary.

candidates.name: Suzanne Bonamici

summary.text: Suzanne Bonamici is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for re-election to Oregon's 1st Congressional District, which she has represented since a 2012 special election. A consumer-protection attorney by training, she served in both chambers of the Oregon Legislature before Congress. Her official biography lists public education as a top priority and describes her as founder and co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional STEAM Caucus.

background.text: Born in Detroit, Michigan, in 1954 according to Ballotpedia; her campaign says she grew up in a small town in Michigan, where her father worked for a local bank and her mother was a small business owner and piano teacher.

Moved to Oregon after high school and worked her way through college, first at Lane Community College (associate degree) and then at the University of Oregon, earning a B.A. in 1980 and a J.D. in 1983.
Worked at Lane County Legal Aid Service during college and law school, then as a consumer protection attorney in the Federal Trade Commission's Credit Practices Division in Washington, D.C.

Moved to Oregon in 1986 with her husband and settled in Washington County, where she practiced law representing individuals and small businesses; took a career break to raise two children and volunteered with education, arts and civic organizations, including the Classroom Law Project and the Beaverton Education Foundation (per her campaign website).
Worked as a legislative assistant in the Oregon House of Representatives in 2001, then was elected in 2006 to House District 34 (Washington County) and served one term (2007-2008).

Was appointed to the Oregon State Senate in 2008, was elected to it, and was re-elected in 2010; she served until 2012, when she won the special election to the U.S. House. In the Legislature she passed a bill to reduce duplicative testing in public schools, according to her congressional biography.

In Congress, serves on the Committee on Education and Workforce (Ranking Member of the Early Childhood, Elementary, and Secondary Education Subcommittee, and a member of the Higher Education and Workforce Development Subcommittee) and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (Subcommittees on Environment and on Investigations and Oversight), per her House committee page.

Her official biography says she played a lead role in the bipartisan Every Student Succeeds Act, served on the Select Committee on the Climate Crisis, and is founder and co-chair of the Congressional STEAM Caucus and co-chair of the House Oceans Caucus and Congressional Estuary Caucus.
Her official biography says she and her husband, Michael, have two grown children.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (Subcommittee on Environment; Subcommittee on Investigations and Oversight) and the Committee on Education and the Workforce.

candidates.researchNotes: Bonamici has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in recent cycles and her campaign site's issues page was not reachable; her House committee lists issue pages for Child Care, Civil Rights, Climate Action, Education, Health Care, Housing and other topics but their text content was not accessible in this pass.

candidates.name: Barbara Kahl

summary.text: Barbara Kahl is the Republican nominee for Oregon's 1st Congressional District. A fourth-generation Oregonian, she worked for about two decades in corporate accounting, finance and purchasing before becoming a veterinarian, and ran a mobile large-animal practice for nearly 20 years. Her campaign materials emphasize jobs and the economy, education, affordability and federal fiscal accountability.

background.text: Describes herself as a fourth-generation Oregonian who worked as a child to help pay for her school clothes; graduated from Hillsboro High School.

Earned a bachelor's degree from Oregon State University in 2001 and a doctorate in veterinary medicine from Oregon State's College of Veterinary Medicine in 2006; says she attended college while raising a family.

Before veterinary medicine, spent about two decades in corporate accounting, finance and purchasing in the frozen food, utilities and high-tech sectors, including at Intel's Hillsboro campus from 1990 to 1997.
Says she traveled with her husband during his military deployments; she and her husband live on farmland in rural Oregon.

Describes herself as a USDA-APHIS nationally accredited veterinarian who spent nearly 20 years running a mobile practice serving large animals, equine, small animals, exotics and livestock across the district.
Says she founded the USPCA nonprofit and rescue organization and received the Oregon Veterinary Medical Association's 2012 Animal Welfare Award.

Serves as a public member of the Oregon Department of Agriculture's CAFO Advisory Committee and has testified before the Oregon Legislature on agriculture, veterinary practice and animal-welfare bills.
Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with 71.5% of the vote over John Verbeek.

priorities.text: Fiscal discipline: cutting federal spending and redundant offices, removing ineligible recipients from benefit programs, and requiring agencies to justify funding or lose it.

Education: revising federal K-12 policy to focus on core academics (math, reading, writing, civics, history, science), restoring PE/music/art for grades K-6, and strengthening special-education support under IDEA.
Government accountability: strict budget discrepancy standards, year-end account closing, public spending reports, and routine forensic financial audits.

positions.summary: Says she supports expanding land and timber use for housing supply, workforce training in the trades, cutting permitting time and costs, and a 'buildable homes' package.
positions.quote: Housing: expanding land/timber use for supply, trades workforce training, cutting permitting time and costs, a "buildable homes" package
